native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: In the 17th century BCE (raw-anchor transition at the BCE 1800→1700 boundary; calendar-century window BCE 1700–1601), Diversity in Pottery Form collapses (ΔZKeform = −1.870 ≈ 1.89σ_form) while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases (ΔZkeverz = +1.450 ≈ 1.58σ_dec) simultaneously — the largest such joint event in the BCE 4100–500 in-range span. Derived directly from capital.csv 100-year anchors (ZKeform, Zkeverz), confirmed on time_series_data.csv PotteryForm_inter/PotteryDecoration_inter, and robust at 0.3σ/0.5σ/1.0σ thresholds. Sign convention: CE = −BCE, so BCE 1800 ↔ CE −1800; N-th century BCE = BCE [N·100, (N−1)·100 + 1].
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Align the two files on 100-year BCE bins using capital.csv as the canonical source of ZKeform (Pottery Form) and Zkeverz (Pottery Decoration); verify CE = −BCE by tying time_series.PotteryForm at CE to capital.ZKeform at BCE for all 37 in-range BCE anchors (BCE 4100..500). 2) Exclude the BCE 4300 and BCE 4200 rows in capital.csv because they sit outside the time_series_data.csv coverage (CE starts at −4100) and form a flat −1.13/−1.92 plateau with no transition signal. 3) Compute raw centennial Δ-step (d_ZKeform, d_Zkeverz) at every BCE anchor; jointly evaluate with multi-thresholds ≥0.3σ/≥0.5σ/≥1.0σ using σ_form=0.989 and σ_dec=0.917 from the in-range raw anchors. 4) Confirm with smoothed _inter series that PotteryForm_inter decreases monotonically and PotteryDecoration_inter increases monotonically across the BCE 1800→1700 boundary. 5) Calendar-century labelling convention: N-th century BCE = BCE [N·100, (N−1)·100 + 1]; report the event as '17th century BCE' (BCE 1700..1601 = CE −1700..−1601) following the researcher instruction. 6) Investigate the BCE 1100→1000 case and explicitly EXCLUDE it as a second-order decorative elevation only (ZKeform stays at the −1.13σ collapse floor; no simultaneous form collapse). 7) Rank simultaneous events by |Δform|+|Δdec|; the BCE 1800→1700 event yields joint score 3.32, the largest non-trivial simultaneous event.

sub_hypo.text: In the 17th century BCE, pottery form diversity collapses while pottery decoration diversity simultaneously increases at the BCE 1800→1700 raw-anchor transition. This is the largest such joint event within BCE 4100–500 and is confirmed by the interpolated series and robust at 0.3σ, 0.5σ, and 1.0σ thresholds.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological capital data aligned on 100-year BCE anchors, using capital.csv as canonical and time_series_data.csv for confirmation. The comparison spans 37 anchors from BCE 4100 to 500; BCE 4300 and 4200 are excluded as outside time-series coverage and a flat plateau without transition signal. The event is labelled 17th century BCE (BCE 1700–1601; CE −1700–−1601), although its raw transition is BCE 1800→1700. CE = −BCE; the N-th century BCE covers BCE N·100 through (N−1)·100 + 1.
sub_hypo.relations: Simultaneous opposing centennial changes: ΔZKeform = −1.870 (approximately −1.89σ_form, with σ_form = 0.989) and ΔZkeverz = +1.450 (approximately +1.58σ_dec, with σ_dec = 0.917), using standard deviations from in-range raw anchors. Both changes meet ≥0.3σ, ≥0.5σ, and ≥1.0σ magnitude thresholds. Across the boundary, PotteryForm_inter decreases monotonically while PotteryDecoration_inter increases monotonically. Ranking simultaneous events by |Δform| + |Δdec| gives 3.32, the largest non-trivial joint event in range. The BCE 1100→1000 decorative increase is excluded because ZKeform remains at the −1.13σ collapse floor without a simultaneous form collapse.
